text: Gold slipped about 0.8% to roughly $3,994, below $4,000 and a three-month low, capping its steepest weekly loss since June.
Silver fell about 1.1% to near $54, its lowest since November 2025; the gold/silver ratio held around 74.
Gold miners fell further than gold: GDX lost about 1.8% and GDXU about 5.7%, as Newmont dropped 3–4% despite a record quarterly profit.
Brent settled up 3.1% at $116.72, its highest since April, on rising Middle East tensions.
Treasury yields bounced back about 5 bp after Thursday's plunge: the 10-year to about 5.00% and the 2-year to about 4.69%.
Stocks slipped again: the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq 0.2%, and the VIX rose to about 20.2.
The yen touched a five-week high before USD/JPY ended little changed near 156.9; the dollar index held near 101.7.
